plan.contextChunk: This figure shows two doubly linked lists and a free list sharing one set of arrays, drawn as a shaded three-row table beside three head pointers. At the left, three labeled boxes give the heads: "free" in a black box holding a white 10, "L2" in a medium gray box holding 9, and "L1" in a light gray box holding 3. To the right sits a black panel with columns numbered 1 through 10 across the top and three rows labeled in italics down the left side: next, key, prev. Every occupied cell is shaded to match the list that owns it. The medium gray cells at indices 9, 7, 1, and 5 carry keys k9, k7, k1, and k5, their next entries reading 7, 1, 5, and a diagonal slash for nil, their prev entries reading slash, 9, 7, and 1. The light gray cells at 3, 6, and 2 hold k3, k6, and k2, with next entries 6, 2, slash and prev entries slash, 3, 6. The black slots at 4, 8, and 10 hold only next values, 8, a slash, and 4, their key and prev cells left empty and cut by dotted white rules. Shading alone separates three structures interleaved across the same index range, and the free chain 10, 4, 8 shows that a slot on the free list needs just one link.

interactions.label: Allocate / Free
interactions.teaches: Allocating removes an index from the free chain and splices it into a list by updating only next/prev pointers; freeing does the reverse — no data moves, only link fields change
Each next or prev value is an index into the same array; hovering makes the pointer's target visually explicit, demystifying the compact tabular representation

demo_steps.title: Three structures, one array
demo_steps.narration: The table stores two doubly linked lists (L1 in light gray, L2 in medium gray) and a free list (black) all in the same next/key/prev arrays. Shading is the only visual cue separating them.

demo_steps.title: Trace L1
demo_steps.narration: Click the L1 head (value 3) to follow the chain 3→6→2→nil. Arrows between next fields show the traversal order through the light-gray cells.

demo_steps.title: Trace L2
demo_steps.narration: Click the L2 head (value 9) to follow 9→7→1→5→nil. Notice these indices are scattered among L1's indices — the lists are fully interleaved in storage.

demo_steps.title: Trace the free list
demo_steps.narration: Click the free head (value 10) to follow 10→4→8→nil. Free slots need only a next pointer; their key and prev cells are unused (shown with dotted rules).

demo_steps.title: Allocate index 10 to L1
demo_steps.narration: Press Allocate: index 10 is removed from the free chain (free head becomes 4, index 4's next becomes 8) and spliced into L1 as the new tail (index 2's next becomes 10, index 10's prev becomes 2). Only four pointer fields change — no data moves.

demo_steps.title: Free index 5 from L2
demo_steps.narration: Press Free: index 5 is unlinked from L2 (index 1's next becomes nil) and pushed onto the free list (free head becomes 5, index 5's next becomes 10). Again, only pointer fields are rewritten.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Array-based linked lists let multiple independent structures share one storage block — allocation and deallocation are pure pointer rewiring, never data movement.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Layout: three head-pointer boxes stacked vertically on the left (free on top in black, L2 middle in medium gray, L1 bottom in light gray), each showing a single integer. To the right, a large black rectangular panel with 10 columns and 3 rows. Column headers 1–10 in white above the panel. Row labels 'next', 'key', 'prev' in white italic to the left of the panel. Cells are color-coded: medium gray for L2 members (indices 9,7,1,5), light gray for L1 members (indices 3,6,2), black for free-list members (indices 10,4,8). Nil pointers drawn as a diagonal slash. Free-list cells have dotted white horizontal lines where key and prev would be, indicating those fields are unused. When tracing (click interaction), draw colored arrows from each next value to the target column header, animating sequentially. For allocate/free button states, animate only the changed cells with a brief flash or color transition.
